analysis: Both changed files are documentation only: docs/developer/test.md (new 'Deadline Admission Estimators' test section, patch head lines 113-138) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (one added row at head line 1687 listing the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES environment variable, forwarded to the daemon, with its source in AdmissionRateEstimators.swift). No code, protocol, key custody, attestation, cache storage, authorization, or encryption behavior is modified in the supplied evidence. The env var appears to be a kill switch for deadline admission estimators. It affects scheduling and admission (availability), not confidentiality or trust decisions. It does not touch the T-041 cache controls, which are the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gate, TTL, HMAC names or account scoping. It does not touch T-053 authorization binding either. The docs state the tests use scripted engines and synthetic data and do not qualify live refusal rates, hardware performance or routing, which is consistent with the threat model's refusal to overclaim. The unverified contract: the referenced Swift source (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift) and the daemon environment-forwarding code were not supplied, so I could not confirm that the variable's semantics are fail-safe or that forwarding it through launchd is consistent with the existing allowlist. The pairing code changes presumably sit in other batches or are outside this evidence. The next pass should check that the forwarded variable cannot affect authorization, attestation or cache scope, and only affects admission timing. No security regression was identified in the docs themselves.
